sections.content:
Population change in South Oxfordshire in 2032

The population in South Oxfordshire is projected to increase from 151,845 people in 2022 to 168,232 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 14,907 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in South Oxfordshire
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In South Oxfordshire, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 250, with 14,597 births and 14,348 deaths in South Oxfordshire between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in South Oxfordshire by 0.2%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 14,907, with 113,269 people moving to the area and 98,362 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Oxfordshire by 9.8%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,050, with 3,393 people moving to the area and 4,442 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in South Oxfordshire by 0.7%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 2,307, with 9,719 people moving to the area and 7,412 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Oxfordshire by 1.5%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in South Oxfordshire in 2032

The median age in South Oxfordshire is projected to rise from 43 years in 2022 to 44 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 23% of the population in South Oxfordshire are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 20% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in South Oxfordshire between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in South Oxfordshire is projected to stay the same, at around 61%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 318 to 343 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in South Oxfordshire?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 22% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in South Oxfordshire between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
